M00551.name: Benzoate degradation, benzoate => catechol / methylbenzoate => methylcatechol

findings.h: Cycloclasticus runs the aromatic response in both winters.
findings.t: Between 85% and 100% of the toluene-monooxygenase, benzene/toluene-dioxygenase, naphthalene-dioxygenase and extradiol-dioxygenase transcripts in the diesel pool come from Cycloclasticus genomes (95% or more for every family except catechol 2,3-dioxygenase, 85–90%). By days 55–82 Cycloclasticus accounts for 19–51% of protein-coding transcripts in diesel-pool water and 12–46% in its ice.

findings.h: Two different Cycloclasticus species bloomed in the two winters.
findings.t: In 2024-25 the bloom was metabat_9342, a genome 98.7% identical to a MAG from Central Arctic Ocean sea ice; it rose mainly after day 20. In 2025-26 it was lorbin_184 (Cycloclasticus sp001566825) and its sibling sub-bins. This species was already in both pools before dosing (0.3–0.6% of binned DNA in the control pool, 1.0–1.8% in the diesel pool). It roughly tripled its share of transcripts within a week of dosing and reached about 20% by day 17. Before dosing, 2025-26 pool water (both pools) already transcribed naphthalene dioxygenase at 26 vs 1.7 CPM and extradiol dioxygenases at 19 vs 1.5 CPM compared with 2024-25 pre-dosing samples. The November 2025 source-water sites carried no Cycloclasticus DNA, so this primed community lived in the pools.

findings.h: Metagenomes confirm the blooms were growth, not just activity.
findings.t: A k-mer screen of 173 CMO Illumina metagenomes follows DNA past the end of nanopore sampling. In the 2024-25 diesel pool, metabat_9342 stays near 0.01% of read k-mers until day 25, then makes up 10–14% of them in water and ice at days 55–63; the control pool stays at 0.01% all season. In 2025-26, lorbin_184 rises from 0.13% before dosing to 0.87% of diesel-pool water k-mers by days 12–25, while the control stays at 0.05–0.08%. The Sphingorhabdus CYP153/alkB plasmid is 10–20× more abundant in diesel-pool DNA than in the control at days 5–25 of 2024-25. Sulfurimonas semibin_088 rises from about 0.01% to 1–3% in the 2024-25 diesel pool, but in 2025-26 it is 3–12% in both pools.

findings.h: Aromatic genes respond more than alkane genes.
findings.t: In 2025-26 seawater, median expression in the diesel pool versus the control (CPM of protein-coding reads) was 42× higher for toluene monooxygenase, 38× for todC, 28× for the extradiol dioxygenases and 16–18× for naphthalene dioxygenase and catechol 2,3-dioxygenase. Corrected for the diesel pool’s own higher pre-dosing level (before-after-control-impact), these responses are 8–18×. Alkane-monooxygenase transcripts rose 3–7×, and much of that signal is divergent alkB-like genes in Cycloclasticus. Curated CANT-HYD profiles assign canonical AlkB mainly to Pseudosulfitobacter. Canonical CYP153 comes mainly from Cycloclasticus metabat_9342 and unbinned Sphingorhabdus in 2024-25, and from unbinned Alcanivorax and Sphingorhabdus in 2025-26.

findings.h: A hydrogen- and sulfur-driven side economy runs alongside.
findings.t: Sulfurimonas carries an H₂- and sulfide-driven, CO₂-fixing metabolism: ATP-citrate lyase (reverse TCA) is 96% Sulfurimonas and pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase 99%. In 2025-26 the two pools started level (Campylobacterota hydrogenase about 2,890 vs 2,820 CPM), then the control fell while the diesel pool held. Measured against each pool’s own baseline, the hydrogenase rose about 9× (+3.2 log₂). In 2024-25 the diesel pool’s single pre-dosing sample was already 13–76× above the control, so that winter’s contrast is mostly pool history. Cycloclasticus joins in during 2025-26 with a bidirectional Hox hydrogenase and nitrate respiration. Sulfate reducers contribute at most 6% of dsrAB transcripts. See the Sulfur & hydrogen page.

findings.h: Short-chain alkane and C1 monooxygenases join in.
findings.t: A copper membrane monooxygenase (pmoA-like) of the Porticoccaceae genome 50-400-T64 reaches a median of about 140 CPM in the 2025-26 diesel pool (rising to about 360 by day 82), against about 2 in the control, with no response in 2024-25. Propane monooxygenase from an unbinned Pseudonocardia contig is 6–10× higher in the 2024-25 diesel pool, but its one pre-dosing diesel-pool sample was already about 5× above the control, so the dosing effect is at most about 1.7×.

Two unlabelled diesel-pool samples from days 62–63, taken after marine oil snow was seen on the pool (day 60), have the highest aromatic-gene expression in the dataset: toluene monooxygenase at 3,300–5,500 CPM and extradiol dioxygenases at 1,200–1,800. That is up to 3× the day 55–60 seawater, and Cycloclasticus makes up 32–51% of their transcripts. In 2025-26 Cycloclasticus is about twice as active in seawater as in ice (no difference in 2024-25), while Oleispira and Sulfurimonas are more active in ice.

findings.h: Gene transfer plays a supporting role, mainly for alkanes.
findings.t: Only 2% of hydrocarbon genes sit on plasmids, phages, islands or integrons, and mobile-associated copies carry about 9% of the diesel-induced transcription in either winter. Cycloclasticus works almost entirely from its chromosome. The clearest mobile actor is a 63.5 kb Sphingorhabdus conjugative plasmid. Its transposon-flanked CYP153 + alkB cassette rises about 60× within a week of dosing, and its DNA depth rises in most diesel-pool runs at days 7–10. Of 6,217 gene pairs shared across contigs at ≥95% amino-acid identity, 26 are flank-confirmed recent transfers between genera. Only 7 of those reach 20 or more reads across all 130 libraries.

findings.h: Metazoan and other eukaryotic transcripts fall.
findings.t: Metazoan signalling and adhesion genes (WIF1, BMP8, protocadherins, mucin), eukaryotic HSP90B, calnexin and mitochondrial ND1 are among the 31 functions that fall more than 2× in every season-by-medium comparison (128 rise). Dinoflagellate, Phaeocystis, cryptophyte and euglenozoan rRNA shares also decline.

caveats.t: Each season had one diesel pool and one control pool, so samples within a pool are repeated measures, not replicates. p- and q-values, including the selection rule in the MAG explorer, compare samples and overstate confidence about pools. 2025-26 has five pre-dosing seawater samples per pool, which allows before-after-control-impact contrasts. 2024-25 has just one pre-dosing seawater RNA sample from the diesel pool (PRE01) and two from the control (PRE01, PRE02), plus the control’s day-5 sample taken the morning of dosing. Neither winter has pre-dosing ice, so ice comparisons cannot be baseline-corrected.

caveats.h: The pools differed before dosing, and not only in diesel
caveats.t: In 2024-25 the two pools were filled about two weeks apart: the intake lines froze during filling, so one pool sat half-full for a couple of weeks before both were topped up. Their communities had diverged before dosing; the diesel pool’s pre-dosing DNA already carried more Sulfitobacter, Sulfurimonas and Casp-alpha2 than the control, and it transcribed far more hydrogenase and nitrogen-uptake genes. In 2025-26 the diesel pool carried about twice the Cycloclasticus of the control (five times as much of lorbin_184, the species that bloomed), more Sulfurimonas (32% vs 24% of binned DNA), and about twice the aromatic-gene transcription. The 2025-26 logs also record the diesel-pool roof open and the control roof closed on several pre-dosing days, so light differed too. Treat raw diesel/control ratios as upper bounds on the diesel effect.

Before dosing, the diesel pool already carried Sulfitobacter, Casp-alpha2 and Sulfurimonas, and the control pool carried Yoonia and UBA5078 instead, so every library can be checked against its pool. In 2024-25 the day-5 extract tubes were exchanged: all five libraries from the control-labelled tube (four nanopore, one Illumina) carry the diesel-pool signature, and the diesel-labelled tube’s RNA, Illumina and three nanopore libraries carry the control markers. These were relabelled. The Illumina PRE02 pair (adjacent wells A03/A04) was also swapped, while the nanopore and RNA libraries of those samples were correct, so only the Illumina pair was relabelled. Two Illumina libraries hold the other pool’s community but have no partner to swap with (EXP_DAY01_SW, EXP_DAY12_SI_TOP), and eight Illumina libraries across both winters failed with under 110,000 read pairs; these are excluded. The two day-18 control libraries and the day-18 ice metagenome are excluded for a different reason, contamination (see below). The corrections live in the metadata archive (sources/sample_corrections.tsv) and are applied by its build scripts. All 2025-26 nanopore, Illumina and RNA libraries match their labels (there the diesel pool carries 4–8× more of the blooming Cycloclasticus relative to its sibling comebin_3787_sub), apart from failed libraries.

caveats.h: Two day-18 control samples were removed
caveats.t: Both control-pool libraries from 2024-25 day 18 (16 December 2024), CMO_CTL_DAY18_SW and CMO_CTL_DAY18_SI, and the Illumina metagenome of the ice core, are excluded from every analysis. They carry a hydrocarbon-degrading community seen on no other control day: Zhongshania aliphaticivorans makes up 20% of the water transcripts and 5.5% of the ice transcripts (at most 0.2% in any other 2024-25 sample), together with Oleispira and Perlucidibaca. Toluene, phenol and naphthalene oxygenase transcripts run higher than in the diesel pool that week. The signal is absent on days 16 and 20 and from the same-day sea foam, and Oleispira is 1.19% of the ice metagenome against 0.01% or less on neighbouring days. This points to contamination during sampling or handling; the field log has no note for that day. The ice library is also technically unusual (4% rRNA against about 50% in its neighbours). The flag is in the metadata archive (sample_corrections.tsv, qc_flag contamination) and is applied wherever samples are selected.

caveats.h: Annotation IDs were out of step
caveats.t: The KEGG and eggNOG annotations in the MAG pipeline output were computed on an earlier gene-calling run whose gene IDs shift partway through the assembly. Every KO here was remapped onto the current genes by identical coordinates; 99.9% of protein-coding genes matched. The KO, COG and CAZy tables from the expression pipeline itself, and the public RNA viewer, still use the misaligned IDs and need regenerating.

In the 2025-26 control pool, 44–78% (median about 62%) of reads assigned to genes hit rRNA, 60% of them one euglenid 18S gene. Expression values use protein-coding genes only, so this costs depth but not accuracy.

About a third of mapped reads fall on contigs outside any MAG. Several highly expressed naphthalene-dioxygenase and extradiol-dioxygenase genes sit on unbinned Cycloclasticus contigs, so per-MAG totals understate the genus.

Only CMO_EXP_DAY04_MOS (2025-26) is logged as suspected marine oil snow. The 2024-25 day 62–63 samples carry no material note; the log records oil snow on the pool surface from day 60. The 136 L diesel volume for 2025-26 is from the CMO 2025 sampling log.

footer: Built 2026-10-23 from danaSeq illumina_rna (strobealign → featureCounts, CDS only) on the marine Flye coassembly; MAGs from DAS Tool; taxonomy GTDB-Tk r226 with Kaiju fallback; DNA abundance from nanopore read mapping. Analysis code: github.com/rec3141/GENICEII.
